transient_retry: one per failed logical request, charged to branch limit

prompts.common: You are working in AppWorld. report_conflict and request_decision send messages to the simulated user in this conversation only. A decision request remains pending without a human reply. For a conflict, give a receipt ID, endpoint and a JSON object with identifying request or result fields. Cite the report or receipt in any decision request. finish_session is the common terminal tool; distinguish done, still pending and waiting. Do not use a bare status to claim success. After a goal change, use the public communication tools whenever useful. Use finish_session to end, or the original supervisor.complete_task if genuinely appropriate. The receipt reference supplied below refers to the last tool result before the new user message.
prompts.procedure: Pause tool submissions whenever the user revises the task. Compare the old and new instructions and verify what actually happened in the tool receipts. A pending request was not submitted. Classify each affected operation and remaining task. Cancel a withdrawn request that has not run. Preserve still-valid work. If a conflicting effect has already happened, promptly report the exact effect and object with its receipt. Repair only with explicit authorization and a feasible exact repair. Otherwise ask what the user authorizes and keep that work paused, without guessing or claiming reversal. An unanswered request is not authorization. Continue independent authorized work while waiting. Follow explicit urgency, importance and dependencies; never run a dependent task before its prerequisite. Check real outcomes before declaring completion.
prompts.assessment: Assess the change before any action. Return JSON exactly {"old":"cancel|keep|unknown","basis":"exact quote from latest user","fix":"exact quote explicitly authorizing repair or empty string","tasks":[]}. old means the last boundary operation is withdrawn, remains wanted, or is uncertain. Its real receipt is already available; never invent an ID. For each independent remaining task, in order, add ["short task","app.api",{"parameter":"literal selector"},"verbatim authorization excerpt",[dependency task positions],priority]. Positions count from 1. A dependency of 0 means pending conflict approval. Priority is 0 unless the user explicitly orders work, then 1 for highest, 2 for next. Use the actual required app and intended write endpoint. Include all user-stated identifying parameters. For a known endpoint requiring an ID not yet visible, use {} and the exact user excerpt. Completed work and the already considered boundary operation need no task card. Leave an empty fix unless the user authorizes reversing this exact committed effect. Keep compact.

function.name: find_api
function.description: Find real AppWorld API names and parameter schemas. Use short keywords or an exact API name.

function.name: call_api
function.description: Execute exactly one documented AppWorld API. The simulator handles login.

function.name: report_conflict
function.description: Tell the user about an actual committed effect that conflicts with the update.

function.name: request_decision
function.description: Ask the simulated user what to do; no reply will be provided in the main study.

function.name: finish_session
function.description: End this session and distinguish done, pending and waiting work.

primary: ARR over every frozen branch, family-matched PACT minus P and A
single_pilot_revision: De-duplicate the boundary operation and its exact inverse. Compare serialized records as lists; allow optional report details when identity fields match.
